newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Phillips/ARCO enter Venezuelan oil exploration.
newsitem.headline: Phillips/ARCO enter Venezuelan oil exploration.

text.p: A 50/50 joint venture between Phillips Petroleum Co and Atlantic Richfield Co said Thursday it aimed to invest $200-300 million over 20 years in the La Vela offshore exploration block in northern Venezuela.

Phillips vice-president Carlos Bustamente hoped to achieve production rates of 20-30,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil and 75 million cubic feet per day of gas, although there were high risks in such a little explored area.

"Clearly there is the opportunity for significant reserves in this area. This is over a million acres with significant potential for oil and gas. It carries with it a lot of risk,+ said Keith Weiser, ARCO's vice-president for Latin America.

The consortium was the sole bidder for the contract in Venezuela's third round of operating licences and paid just $1 million. Previous bids for 13 operating contracts have netted almost $2 billion for Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA).
The La Vela offshore block, located near the Falcon peninsula in northern Venezuela, was offered in a previous contracting round, but received no offers.

The area has proven reserves of 54 million barrels, but no previous commercial production. If commercially viable reserves are found, the area would require significant infrastructure investment as none exists currently.
PDVSA production chief Vicenzo Paglione said Venezuela would provide an immediate market for gas, were it found in the block, in the form of its huge refining operations on the peninsula.
Phillips and ARCO are both existing partners with PDVSA in an extra-heavy Orinoco oil venture, and both have won operating contracts earlier in the five-day round.
